title: Supervisor race and restart hardening gate
description: Objective: closing hardening gate for the external effect supervisor slice; carries the parent task's full DoD evidence (task-312c1de3c76a4f1dbd8da5c34e629b0e). SPIDR child 4 of 4, split per human-approved 4-child decomposition 2026-08-08. This is the epic-verification-budget FINAL task for the slice: it owns full regression, the whole-slice adversarial pass, and the docs sweep — mid-slice children deliberately ran focused gates only. Deliverable: a seeded deterministic race harness across claim/activate/cancel/duplicate-delivery/restart orderings spanning runner supervisor and daemon work services, following the lease-presence-core harness pattern (multiple seeds x hundreds of steps, honest/tamper bias, and the test asserts the observed outcome-kind SET equals an exact expected list with per-kind counts recorded — see mem:task-task-967769ea801f4fe09944e4fdcc47663e-handoff for the shape and non-vacuity bar); cross-package invariant checks proving parent DoD 1-3 end to end: no external-action grant precedes a committed ARMED->ACTIVE + LAUNCH_REQUESTED->RUNNING pair on ANY seeded schedule; every race ends in one legal state with token/epoch/budget/runtime closure revalidated; duplicate delivery never blind-relaunches. Full regression: both focused gates plus repo root pnpm test. Whole-slice adversarial review and docs sweep (inline why-comments; no new docs/ contract unless a public surface changed). NOT in scope: new supervisor/service features — this task adds tests and fixes only defects those tests expose (defect fixes stay within the slice's owned paths and must each get a red-first test). Hard dependencies: children 1-3 (task-2580a578, task-4a3b5ec0, task-ba3a45f9) all DONE. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/supervisor/** and apps/daemon/src/work/** (test additions plus defect fixes only). Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm test.
definitionOfDone: The race harness runs >=5 seeds x >=200 steps per seed with a documented honest/tamper bias and asserts the observed outcome-kind set EQUALS an exact expected list (no unexpected kind, no missing kind); per-kind counts are recorded in the test output and quoted in the completion evidence.

Across every seeded schedule, no external-action grant is observed before its committed ARMED->ACTIVE + LAUNCH_REQUESTED->RUNNING pair, and no duplicate delivery produces a fresh launch — both asserted as harness invariants, not spot checks.

Start/cancel/release/restart races end in exactly one legal state with current token, epoch, budget, and runtime closure revalidated; the harness asserts version-delta and strongest-reason monotonicity invariants on every step.
Any defect found gets a red-first focused test and a fix within the slice's owned paths; zero regressions: both focused gates AND repo root pnpm test exit 0 with fresh output quoted.
Adversarial self-review checklist run on the whole slice; no probe, scratch, or debug files committed; only owned paths staged and committed.
taskRails: This gate concentrates verification: do not weaken it into spot checks; the outcome-kind set equality and nonzero per-kind counts are the non-vacuity bar (a sweep producing zero cases must fail).
Determinism: seeds are pinned constants; no Date.now or Math.random outside the seeded generator; identical reruns produce identical outcome counts.
Fix defects red-first inside owned paths; anything outside the slice's ownership is a report to #architects, not an edit.
Keep each test file <=400 lines, split by concern before that. Commit by explicit pathspec only.
Assert reason codes and refusing layers throughout; the harness must assert against production surfaces, never a reimplementing helper.

implementationPlan.description: Build the seeded harness engine — pure, dependency-free, and buildable regardless of children 2-3. Create packages/runner/src/supervisor/race-harness.ts following the lease-core pattern in mem:task-task-967769ea801f4fe09944e4fdcc47663e-handoff: a deterministic PRNG seeded from a FIXED LITERAL seed array (no Math.random, no clock anywhere, so every failing schedule is reproducible); a command alphabet covering claim, arm, activate, requestCancel, settle, consumeGrant, tombstone, duplicate-delivery, restart and drain; an asserted-good state pool of at least five members so the schedule explores real states rather than one; a documented honest/tamper bias (the lease core used 70/30 — document whatever you choose); and an outcome recorder that accumulates observed outcome KINDS with PER-KIND COUNTS. The recorder is the load-bearing part: it must expose both the observed kind set and the counts, because DoD 1 requires set equality against a hand-written list AND counts quoted in the evidence.
implementationPlan.note: Harness engine built as three focused modules (split for the per-file cap, all well under 250 lines): race-harness.ts (xorshift PRNG seeded from the fixed literal RACE_SEEDS=[3,11,29,61,127], RACE_STEPS=240, documented 70/30 HONEST_IN_TEN bias, OutcomeRecorder with per-kind counts + undeclared-kind throw, StepRecord/RaceEvent, checkGrantOrdering, runTrace); race-world.ts (10-command alphabet, World, 5-member asserted-good statePool built by real applyEffectCommand/activateEffect transitions, per-command honest+tamper application); race-scenarios.ts (stratified hand-written drain/restart input pools + 16 activation leg tampers). No Date.now, no Math.random, no clock. `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` exit 0.

implementationPlan.description: Test the harness itself, because a harness nobody checks is the easiest place for this whole gate to become vacuous. Create packages/runner/src/supervisor/race-harness.test.ts asserting: the same seed produces the identical schedule twice (reproducibility — without it a failure cannot be investigated); different seeds produce different schedules (the seed is actually used); the requested step count is actually executed rather than short-circuited; the tamper bias produces both honest and tampered commands in roughly the documented proportion, asserting BOTH are non-zero so a bias of 100/0 cannot pass; and the outcome recorder counts what it observes, verified by feeding it a known sequence and asserting exact counts. Also assert the harness fails loudly on an unknown outcome kind rather than dropping it, since a silently ignored kind would defeat the set-equality assertion this gate is built on.
implementationPlan.note: race-harness.test.ts: 17 tests, all green. Covers reproducibility (same seed = identical trace), seed sensitivity (different seed = different trace), seeded(0) throws on the xorshift fixed point, exact requested step count with ordered indices, whole command alphabet drawn, honest AND tampered counts both non-zero plus the 70/30 proportion held within 0.6-0.8, the 5-member asserted-good pool states, grant present only on the ACTIVE member, recorder exact per-kind counts on a known sequence, recorder THROWS on an undeclared kind, recorder hands back a defensive copy, and five load-bearing checks on checkGrantOrdering fed deliberately broken synthetic logs (reordered launch, forged grant id, half pair, null pair). Also split the engine to hold the <=250 per-file target: race-harness.ts 192, race-world.ts 140, race-steps.ts 259, race-scenarios.ts 164, race-restart-scenarios.ts 146. Added StepOutcome.outcomeKind carrying the production surface's own `kind` verbatim so a test can compare against a frozen exported vocabulary rather than a label the harness invented.

TWO HARNESS DEFECTS THE GATE CAUGHT ON ITS FIRST RED RUN, both fixed:
1. xorshift32 low-bit correlation. Every decision is `value % n` for small n and each step draws three in a row; xorshift is linear so those low bits stay linearly related. Three of the 16 activation leg tampers were NEVER reached and two more fired once in 1200 steps - i.e. the gate was silently narrower than it claimed. Replaced with splitmix32 (mixed counter, full avalanche) and added a self-test asserting a 16-way split two draws after a 10-way split reaches all 16 arms.
2. Grant provenance gap. The ACTIVE pool member holds a grant committed before step 0, so an honest consume recorded a LAUNCH with no in-log issuance and checkGrantOrdering fired. Not a production defect - the grant is real. Fixed by priming the event log from the pool, but ONLY for members whose three records the production validateActivationCommit agrees are a whole commit; an incoherent one stays unrecorded so a launch off it still fails.

implementationPlan.description: Assert the parent slice's headline safety property — DoD 2, the one the whole supervisor exists to guarantee. In supervisor-races.test.ts add two harness-level invariants checked on every seeded schedule, not as spot checks. First: NO external-action grant is ever observed before its committed ARMED->ACTIVE plus LAUNCH_REQUESTED->RUNNING pair. Implement this as a running check over the recorded step log so a violation anywhere in any schedule fails, and verify the check is load-bearing by temporarily reordering a synthetic log and confirming it goes red — an invariant that never fires on a deliberately broken input is not testing anything. Second: NO duplicate delivery ever produces a fresh launch; every duplicate resolves to ADOPTED, EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH or SUSPECT, asserted by set equality against child 2's exported frozen kind list so a blind-relaunch kind cannot appear unnoticed.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 2 asserted as harness invariants over every seeded schedule (supervisor-races.test.ts "DoD 2" block, 5 tests).

First invariant - no external-action grant before its committed pair. checkGrantOrdering runs over the whole recorded event log of each of the 8 seeds and must return []. It flags three distinct faults: a grant minted by anything other than the exact ARMED->ACTIVE|LAUNCH_REQUESTED->RUNNING pair, a launch of a grant no activation minted, and a launch whose step index precedes its issuance. A separate test asserts activations AND launches are both non-zero (19 activations, 73 world-provenance launches across the run) so the invariant is not passing on an empty set.

Rewrote the check to two passes while wiring this up: the single-pass version compared each launch only against issuances EARLIER IN THE ARRAY, which made it an assertion about the log's sort order rather than about the schedule, and left its own index-comparison branch unreachable. Collecting all issuances first makes the step-index property the thing under test.

Load-bearing verification (race-harness.test.ts, 5 tests on deliberately broken synthetic logs): a correct log returns []; the same two events with the launch at step 1 and its activation at step 4 returns exactly "step 1: launch precedes its activation at step 4"; a forged grant id returns "step 9: launch of grant-forged that no activation minted"; a half pair (LAUNCH_REQUESTED->LAUNCH_REQUESTED) and a null pair each return an "uncommitted pair" violation.

Second invariant - duplicate delivery never blind-relaunches. Set EQUALITY of the observed outcomeKind values on duplicateDelivery steps against child 2's exported frozen DUPLICATE_DELIVERY_KINDS (ADOPTED | EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH | SUSPECT), using the production surface's own `kind` rather than a label the harness invented, so a fourth optimistic arm cannot hide behind "every observed kind is one we declared". Plus a per-seed check that no LAUNCH event ever shares a step index with a duplicateDelivery step, with a non-zero duplicate-step count asserted first. Observed: ADOPTED 83, EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH 50, SUSPECT 155 (66 LAUNCH_LOCK_SUSPECT + 34 REGISTRATION_ABSENT + 26 IDENTITY_CONFLICT + 29 MALFORMED). 32/32 tests green.

implementationPlan.description: Restart reconstruction races — DoD 3's restart half. Create packages/runner/src/supervisor/supervisor-restart.test.ts seeding crash points across the slice's transaction boundaries and asserting that reconstruction lands each pre-crash state in EXACTLY ONE legal post state, compared against a hand-written expected outcome set asserted for set equality and non-zero length. Assert that current token, epoch, budget and runtime closure are revalidated after every restart — a reconstruction that restores state without re-proving authority is the defect this DoD names. Assert no premature terminal: a terminal label must never appear where its evidence is absent, and the restart path must prefer UNKNOWN or SUSPECT over a guessed terminal. Include the composed case none of the individual drills cover: a restart landing mid-drain, which must remain DRAINING with its holds intact rather than resolving optimistically.
implementationPlan.note:
supervisor-restart.test.ts: 39 tests green. 19 hand-written crash points spanning the slice's transaction boundaries (pre-attempt, post-claim, post-arm, post-launch-request, BOTH halves of a split activation commit, a non-deriving grant id, whole commit x lock HELD/RELEASED/UNKNOWN, observation without registration, three mid-drain variants, post-tombstone, terminal attempt over a live effect, and three settled-effect evidence levels). Each asserted against its own hand-written label, then the produced answer set asserted for set EQUALITY against a hand-written 11-entry list with non-zero length, and all 7 RESTART_POST_STATES asserted reached so none is dead vocabulary.

Authority is re-proved, not restored, asserted in two halves: (a) structurally, every RECONSTRUCTED outcome's own keys are exactly [capacityHeld, kind, ok, postState, terminalTarget] - no grant, no lease, no token, so a reconstruction cannot hand back authority; (b) behaviourally, five post-restart re-activations over the rehydrated records are each refused with a NAMED code AND layer - LEASE_MIRROR_STALE/LEASE_MIRROR (token), LEASE_MIRROR_STALE_EPOCH/LEASE_MIRROR (epoch), LEASE_MIRROR_SUPERSEDED_AUTHORITY/LEASE_MIRROR, PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED/ACTIVATION (runtime closure), ACTIVATION_GRAPH_EPOCH_MISMATCH/ACTIVATION - plus a positive control asserting the same base request DOES commit, so the five refusals cannot all be a broken fixture. Grant-id re-derivation checked by forging the id on an otherwise whole commit.

Budget/capacity closure: a hand-written postState -> capacityHeld table checked against every crash point (ACTIVE_ADOPTED and DRAINING hold; TERMINAL_PROVEN, TOMBSTONED, RECONCILE_ONLY, SUSPECT, UNKNOWN do not). The composed mid-drain case asserts DRAINING with capacityHeld true and terminalTarget null.

No premature terminal: four unproven-evidence cases must land inside a written-out admitted set. Fixed a weak assertion caught while writing it - the first draft mapped any refusal onto "post:UNKNOWN" before comparing, so it passed for ANY refusal; it now compares the real label against the explicit four-member admitted list. Also asserts RESTART_PREMATURE_TERMINAL and RESTART_SAFE_HANDOFF_ABSENT each name the RESTART layer, distinguishing the latter from the identical fact refused at DRAIN. Redaction asserted: no crash-point answer echoes the lease token or the bootstrap credential digest.

implementationPlan.description: The cross-package drift test, which MUST live in the daemon — child 1 deferred it here for a structural reason. @moe/runner depends only on @moe/contracts, so a runner test cannot import @moe/scheduler and therefore cannot compare the supervisor's `lease-mirror.ts` against the real `fenceAuthority`. apps/daemon has @moe/scheduler and gains @moe/runner through child 3's approved ownership amendment, so it is the only place both surfaces meet. Create apps/daemon/src/work/work-races.test.ts asserting VERDICT EQUALITY, not merely 'both refuse': for a shared table of hostile and honest lease inputs, the supervisor's mirrored validation and the scheduler's fenceAuthority must return the SAME verdict and the SAME reason code on every case. Assert the case count is non-zero and that both accepting and refusing verdicts appear, so a table that only ever refuses cannot pass. Also drive child 3's work services through the harness for the claim/activate orderings that span both packages.

Fix the defects the harness exposes — DoD 4, and the reason this gate exists. Every fix is red-first: add the focused failing test that names the defect, then make the minimum change, and keep the fix in a separate commit-visible shape from the harness code so the diff shows what the harness caught. Fixes stay strictly INSIDE the slice's owned paths (packages/runner/src/supervisor/** and apps/daemon/src/work/**); a defect found in a foreign package is REPORTED, not fixed here. Add no features — this task adds tests and defect fixes only, and new supervisor, relay or service surface belongs in a new task. If the harness exposes NO defect, say so explicitly in the completion evidence together with the seeds, step counts and per-kind coverage that justify the claim — a negative result is a result, but a gate narrowed until it produces one violates the slice's own rail.
implementationPlan.note:
NO PRODUCTION DEFECT FOUND in children 1-2, and the negative result is justified by numbers rather than asserted: 8 seeds x 400 steps = 3200 steps over a 10-command alphabet and a 5-member asserted-good state pool, 70/30 honest/tamper, reaching all 66 declared outcome kinds with every kind hit >=3 times (full count table in the step-4 note). Zero versionDelta violations, zero input mutations, zero monotonicity violations, zero grant-ordering violations, zero duplicate-delivery relaunches.

TWO DEFECTS THE GATE DID EXPOSE, both in the harness, both fixed red-first (the failing run came first in each case):
1. xorshift32 low-bit correlation silently narrowed the gate. Three of the 16 activation leg tampers were never reached and two more fired once in 1200 steps, so five refusal codes were effectively untested while the suite looked green. Replaced with splitmix32 and added a self-test asserting a 16-way split taken two draws after a 10-way split reaches all 16 arms.
2. checkGrantOrdering compared each launch only to issuances EARLIER IN THE ARRAY, making it an assertion about log sort order rather than about step index, and leaving its own index-comparison branch unreachable. Rewritten as two passes; the reordered-log self-test now genuinely exercises the index comparison.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) THIS IS THE ONE TASK IN THE BATCH THAT CANNOT BE FULLY DE-BLOCKED BY CLEVERNESS, AND PRETENDING OTHERWISE WOULD BE THE WORST OUTCOME. It is a hardening gate: its entire product is tests over children 1-3's code. Child 1 is real (11 files, untracked); at plan time child 2 had produced ZERO files and child 3 had no plan. A gate written against absent code would be a weakened gate, and the parent slice's own rail says a drill weakened, skipped, or narrowed to pass defeats the purpose of the whole SPIDR breakdown. So this plan does NOT fake coverage.
(2) WHAT IT DOES INSTEAD — it splits into two halves along the dependency line. The HARNESS ENGINE (seeded scheduler, command alphabet, outcome recorder, per-kind counting, set-equality assertion) is pure, depends on nothing from children 2-3, and is fully buildable and testable today. The SLICE INVARIANTS need the slice. Building the engine first is real progress that is never wasted, and it front-loads the part that historically takes longest to get right. By queue order this task is claimed last, so children 1-3 will most likely be DONE by then and the plan runs straight through; step 1 decides which world you are in.
(3) FOLLOW THE LEASE-CORE HARNESS, DO NOT INVENT ONE. `mem:task-task-967769ea801f4fe09944e4fdcc47663e-handoff` gives the exact shape AND the non-vacuity bar to beat: 5 seeds x 240 steps, a 5-member asserted-good state pool, 70/30 honest/tamper bias, a 10-command alphabet, and a test asserting the observed outcome-kind SET equals an exact 18-entry list with per-kind counts recorded. That memory's count table is the model for what this task must quote in its own evidence.
(4) THE DRIFT TEST GOES IN THE DAEMON, NOT THE RUNNER. Runner tests cannot import @moe/scheduler (@moe/runner depends only on @moe/contracts). The supervisor's `lease-mirror.ts` re-validates at fenceAuthority strictness, and proving the mirror has not drifted from the real `fenceAuthority` requires both in one place — that is apps/daemon, which has @moe/scheduler and gains @moe/runner via child 3's approved ownership amendment. planningNotes.risks:
1. **The gate must not be weakened to go green.** If children 2-3 are still absent when this is claimed, do NOT trim the expected outcome-kind list to whatever the harness happens to produce — that inverts the entire point, since DoD 1's set-equality assertion is only meaningful against a HAND-WRITTEN expected list. Build the engine, then wait or block on the slice arms.
2. `mem:gotcha-self-derived-universe-cannot-check-itself` is the central trap here: an expected outcome-kind list derived from a harness run cannot check that run. Write the expected list BY HAND from the design and the children's exported vocabularies, and let the test fail loudly when reality disagrees — that failure is the gate doing its job.
3. **Non-vacuity has a numeric bar**: DoD 1 demands >=5 seeds x >=200 steps with a documented honest/tamper bias and per-kind counts quoted in the evidence. A harness that runs the required steps but explores one state is vacuous — the lease core beat this with a 5-member asserted-good state pool and a 10-command alphabet. Record per-kind counts and treat any kind with count 0 as a coverage failure to investigate, not a pass.
4. **No clock, no randomness outside the seeded PRNG.** Seeds are a fixed literal array so any failure is reproducible; a non-reproducible failing schedule is not a bug report. No Date.now, no Math.random.
5. **Defect fixes are in scope but features are not.** Every fix needs a red-first focused test and must stay inside the slice's owned paths. Resist fixing anything in a foreign package — report it instead.
6. **This task runs repo-root `pnpm test`.** Attribute red by path and never by a remembered count; a stale 'known failures' number is exactly the false baseline that had to be retracted from another plan on this board today. Investigate anything outside the slice before calling it foreign.
7. **Commit hazard**: `packages/runner/src/supervisor/` is shared and was full of untracked foreign files at plan time. Commit by explicit per-file pathspec only, never the directory.
